entity: AT: constitutional court (Verfassungsgerichtshof)
notes: Art. 147(1) B-VG: President, Vice-President and twelve further members = 14 members proper. Six substitute members (Ersatzmitglieder) exist separately and are not added. Court's own page describes the plenum as the President, the Vice-President and 'the other twelve members'. Members need not be career judges; proposed by the Federal Government (6 members + 3 substitutes), the Nationalrat (3 + 2) and the Bundesrat (3 + 1).

entity: BE: constitutional court (Cour constitutionnelle / Grondwettelijk Hof)
notes: Court: 'The Court is composed of twelve judges' - six Dutch-language and six French-language, one of whom must have adequate knowledge of German; per linguistic group three appointed for legal experience and three for at least five years' parliamentary experience. Appointed for life by the King. Legal basis: Art. 142 of the Constitution and the Special Act of 6 January 1989 on the Constitutional Court.

entity: BG: constitutional court (Конституционен съд)
notes: Court: 'The Constitutional Court is composed of twelve justices.' One third elected by the National Assembly, one third appointed by the President, one third elected by the General Assembly of the judges of the Supreme Court of Cassation and the Supreme Administrative Court (Art. 147(1) of the Constitution). The Court elects its Chairman for a three-year term.

entity: HR: constitutional court (Ustavni sud)
notes: Court: 'The Constitutional Court consists of thirteen judges elected by the Croatian Parliament for a term of eight years from among notable jurists.' Constitution Art. 122 of the consolidated text of 15 January 2014 (numbered Art. 125 in the OG 76/10 consolidation) likewise fixes thirteen justices. Judges elected by a two-thirds majority of all MPs.

entity: CY: constitutional court (Supreme Constitutional Court)
notes: Court's Annual Review 2024: with the Reform Laws the former Supreme Court of thirteen Justices was divided into a Supreme Constitutional Court and a Supreme Court, 'consisting of nine and seven Justices, respectively'. Ministry of Justice (gov.cy courts-reform page) states 'Supreme Constitutional Court (composed of 9 judges)'. The Supreme Constitutional Court was created by the 2022 judicial-reform laws and became operative on 1 July 2023, taking over the Supreme Court's constitutional jurisdiction.

entity: CZ: constitutional court (Ústavní soud)
notes: Court: 'The Constitutional Court consists of the President, two Vice-Presidents, and other twelve Justices' = 15. Legal basis: Art. 84 of the Constitutional Charter (15 Justices, appointed by the President with the consent of the Senate) and Act No. 182/1993 Coll. on the Constitutional Court.

entity: DK: constitutional court (none; review by the ordinary courts, ultimately Højesteret)
notes: No separate constitutional court. The Ministry of Justice lists the ordinary courts exhaustively: Højesteret, landsretterne, byretterne, Sø- og Handelsretten and Tinglysningsretten, plus Grønlands Domstole, Retten på Færøerne and Den Særlige Klageret; no constitutional court appears. Constitutional review is diffuse and exercised by the ordinary courts. The Danish Courts' own site (domstol.dk) sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be saved.

entity: EE: constitutional court (none; Riigikohus - Supreme Court, Constitutional Review Chamber)
notes: No separate constitutional court. The Supreme Court (Riigikohus) hears 'petitions for constitutional review' through its Constitutional Review Chamber, one of four chambers (Civil, Criminal, Administrative Law, Constitutional Review). The Court has 19 justices in total (riigikohus.ee justices page), so constitutional review is concentrated inside the ordinary supreme court rather than in a dedicated constitutional court.

entity: FI: constitutional court (none; Constitutional Law Committee of Parliament and the courts)
notes: No constitutional court. Constitution of Finland s.74: Parliament's Constitutional Law Committee gives opinions on the constitutionality of legislative proposals and their relation to international human rights treaties. s.106: where applying a statutory provision would be in evident conflict with the Constitution, the court must give precedence to the Constitution. Review is therefore ex ante political and ex post diffuse.

entity: FR: constitutional council (Conseil constitutionnel)
notes: Art. 56: 'The Constitutional Council shall comprise nine members' - three appointed by the President of the Republic, three by the President of the National Assembly and three by the President of the Senate; nine-year non-renewable term, one third renewed every three years. Former Presidents of the Republic are ex officio life members and are NOT included in the value of 9.

entity: DE: constitutional court (Bundesverfassungsgericht)
notes: Court: 'The Federal Constitutional Court consists of two Senates with eight Justices each' and refers to 'the 16 Justices'. s.2 BVerfGG: two Senates, eight judges elected to each. Half of the Justices are elected by the Bundestag and half by the Bundesrat; at least three Justices of each Senate must come from the supreme federal courts.

entity: GR: constitutional court (none; diffuse review by all courts; Special Highest Court under Art. 100)
notes: No constitutional court. Art. 93(4): the courts are bound not to apply a statute whose content is contrary to the Constitution (diffuse review). The Special Highest Court (Art. 100) is not a constitutional court: its jurisdiction is objections under Art. 58, verification of referendum validity, MP incompatibility or forfeiture, conflicts between courts and administrative authorities, conflicts between the supreme courts on the constitutionality or interpretation of a statute, and designation of generally acknowledged rules of international law. Its composition (Art. 100(2)) is 11 members - the three supreme court presidents plus four councillors of the Council of State and four judges of the Supreme Civil and Criminal Court - expanded by two law professors in certain cases; not recorded as a constitutional-court figure.

entity: HU: constitutional court (Alkotmánybíróság)
notes: Court: 'The fifteen members of the Court are elected by the Parliament with qualified majority (the vote of two-thirds of all representatives) for a term of twelve years.' Legal basis: Art. 24(1) of the Fundamental Law (fifteen members) and Act CLI of 2011 on the Constitutional Court. The Court decides in plenary sessions, five-member panels or as a single judge.

entity: IE: constitutional court (none; High Court and Supreme Court)
notes: No separate constitutional court. The Supreme Court 'sits at the top of the Irish courts system and is the court of final appeal in civil and criminal matters. It also has the final say in respect of the interpretation of Ireland's basic law, Bunreacht na hEireann (the Constitution of Ireland)'. Constitutional review is exercised by the ordinary courts (High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court under Art. 34 of the Constitution); no dedicated constitutional court statute exists.

entity: IT: constitutional court (Corte costituzionale)
notes: Costituzione art. 135(1): 'La Corte costituzionale è composta di quindici giudici', one third appointed by the President of the Republic, one third by Parliament in joint session, one third by the supreme ordinary and administrative courts. Figure taken from the Court's own PDF of the Constitution. Current membership not checked: the Court's composition pages (actionComposizione.do) return a Radware CAPTCHA from this network, so vacancies cannot be ruled out.

entity: LV: constitutional court (Satversmes tiesa)
notes: Satversmes tiesas likums (Constitutional Court Law) art. 3: 'Satversmes tiesā ir septiņi tiesneši' - seven judges. Satversme art. 85 leaves the composition to statute and provides that judges are confirmed by the Saeima by not less than 51 votes. Current membership not verified: satv.tiesa.gov.lv did not complete TLS from this network.

entity: LT: constitutional court (Konstitucinis Teismas)
notes: Constitution art. 103: 'Konstitucinį Teismą sudaro 9 teisėjai', appointed for nine years and for one term only, one third renewed every three years; three candidates each nominated by the President, the Seimas Speaker and the Supreme Court President and appointed by the Seimas. Page published by the Seimas; saved copy converted from Windows-1257 to UTF-8.

entity: LU: constitutional court (Cour constitutionnelle)
notes: Ministry of Justice page: composed of the President of the Cour supérieure de justice, the President of the Cour administrative, two conseillers à la Cour de cassation and five magistrats appointed by the Grand Duke = 9 members; a chamber sits with five judges. Legal basis: loi du 27 juillet 1997 (linked on the page as 'Références légales'); the constitutional article could not be read because legilux.public.lu serves only a JavaScript shell and cour-constitutionnelle.lu does not resolve. The nine members listed as current match the statutory number.

entity: MT: Constitutional Court (Qorti Kostituzzjonali)
notes: Constitution art. 95(2): 'One of the Superior Courts, composed of such three judges as could, in accordance with any law for the time being in force in Malta, compose the Court of Appeal, shall be known as the Constitutional Court'. Not a separate court: it is a division of the Superior Courts sitting with three judges. Text is the official English version published by the Legislation Division.

entity: NL: no constitutional court; judicial review barred (Grondwet art. 120)
notes: No constitutional court. Grondwet art. 120: 'De rechter treedt niet in de beoordeling van de grondwettigheid van wetten en verdragen' - courts may not review the constitutionality of statutes and treaties. Review substitutes: statutes may be disapplied where incompatible with directly binding treaty provisions (art. 94), lower regulations are reviewable by courts, and constitutional scrutiny is ex ante via the Council of State (Raad van State) and the Commission for Legislation.

entity: PL: constitutional court (Trybunał Konstytucyjny)
notes: Constitution art. 194(1): 'Trybunał Konstytucyjny składa się z 15 sędziów, wybieranych indywidualnie przez Sejm na 9 lat'. Vacancies: the Court's 'Sędziowie Trybunału' page (list current at 2 November 2026) shows 10 sitting judges - Bentkowska, Patyra, Piotrowicz, Sochański, Stelina, Sych, Szostek, Święczkowski, Wojciechowski, Wyrembak - i.e. 5 of the 15 seats unfilled. Value recorded is the statutory figure, not the sitting count.

entity: PT: constitutional court (Tribunal Constitucional)
notes: Constituição art. 222(1): 'O Tribunal Constitucional é composto por treze juízes', ten elected by the Assembleia da República and three co-opted. The Court's 'Juízes > Plenário' page (composition from June 2026) lists 13 judges, so no vacancy. Constitution text is the consolidated version published by the Assembleia da República.

entity: RO: constitutional court (Curtea Constituţională)
notes: Constitution art. 142(2): 'Curtea Constituţională se compune din nouă judecători, numiţi pentru un mandat de 9 ani'; three appointed by the Chamber of Deputies, three by the Senate, three by the President (art. 142(3)). Text as republished after Legea de revizuire 429/2003, published by the Camera Deputaţilor. Current membership not checked: ccr.ro returns HTTP 503 / a JavaScript interstitial from this network.

entity: SK: constitutional court (Ústavný súd)
notes: Constitution art. 134(1): 'Ústavný súd sa skladá z trinástich sudcov'. Vacancy: the Court's 'Sudcovia' page (last updated 10 July 2026) lists 12 sitting judges, so one of the 13 seats is unfilled. Text is the slov-lex consolidated version effective 1 January 2025, which already carries the current appointment rules.

entity: SI: constitutional court (Ustavno sodišče)
notes: Government portal (gov.si): 'Ustavno sodišče sestavlja devet sodnikov, ki jih na predlog predsednika republike izvoli državni zbor' - nine judges elected by the National Assembly on the proposal of the President for nine years, without re-election (Constitution art. 163). The Court's own site us-rs.si returns HTTP 403 to this network, so current membership was not checked.

entity: ES: constitutional court (Tribunal Constitucional)
notes: Ley Orgánica 2/1979 art. 5(1): 'El Tribunal Constitucional está integrado por doce miembros, con el título de Magistrados del Tribunal Constitucional'; Constitution art. 159 provides 12 members, four proposed by the Congress, four by the Senate, two by the Government and two by the CGPJ. Consolidated text on the BOE. Current membership not checked: tribunalconstitucional.es returns HTTP 403.

entity: SE: no constitutional court; decentralised review (Regeringsformen 11 kap. 14 §)
notes: No constitutional court. Regeringsformen 11 kap. 14 §: a court that finds a provision contrary to a constitutional or other superior statute must not apply it (lagprövning), giving particular weight to the Riksdag's position as the people's foremost representative and to the primacy of constitutional law. Constitutional scrutiny is otherwise ex ante by the Council on Legislation (Lagrådet, RF 8 kap.).

entity: AT: full professors of law (BMBWF — Statistisches Taschenbuch Hochschulen und Forschung 2025)
notes: Table 5.1 'Personal an Universitaeten' reports professors only as an all-discipline total (3,257 professors at public universities, 2024) and Table 5.2 breaks that down by university, not by field of law. Statistik Austria's open-data catalogue (data.statistik.gv.at) carries no university-personnel dataset by ISCED-F field; the 'Personal an Universitaeten' breakdown by field is not publicly downloadable.

entity: BE: full professors of law (Statbel — Direction générale Statistique; Flemish and French Community education statistics)
notes: No official Belgian statistic publishes university professors split by legal discipline. Statbel's education theme covers enrolments and qualifications, not academic staff by field. The Flemish 'Onderwijs in cijfers' portal returns a JavaScript shell to non-browser clients, and the Federation Wallonia-Brussels statistics portal refused automated access ('Requete non autorisee', bot block); absence of a law-level figure could therefore not be verified for the French Community.

entity: BG: full professors of law (Национален статистически институт)
notes: NSI higher-education domain publishes three tables only: institutions by type; enrolled students and graduates by statistical region; academic staff by post, sex, employment type and ownership. Professors 2025/2026 = 2,360 (1,656 full-time), all fields. No professional-field (Право) breakdown is published.

entity: CY: academic staff with a law qualification
notes: All academic and teaching staff whose highest qualification is in law, all ranks; no professor-only split. 'Mapping of the Higher Education Field in Cyprus 2023-2024', Table 42, row 9 'Nomiki' (law): 218 staff (universities 166, colleges 52), 4.6% of 4,692 staff with valid field data, academic year 2023-2024, headcount. Classification is by the field of the person's highest educational qualification, not by faculty of employment, and the table is not cross-tabulated with rank. For reference, the same report (Table 45) gives 688 professors nationally, all fields. CYSTAT publishes tertiary personnel with no field dimension.

entity: CZ: full professors of law (Ministerstvo školství, mládeže a tělovýchovy)
notes: MŠMT publishes a staff yearbook whose university section (B1.6 'Vysoké školství – vysoké školy', file id 64441 of the 2024 edition) is the table that would carry pedagogical staff by faculty and academic rank; its binary could not be obtained. The migrated msmt.gov.cz serves attachments through a client-side application (every /file/<id>/download request returns the SPA shell, no archive copy exists in the Wayback Machine), and statis.msmt.gov.cz covers students/graduates only. Law faculties could therefore not be summed.

entity: DK: professors of law (not separable in official statistics)
notes: Value left blank: the published figure is 5,741 scientific staff in the social-sciences field, all ranks; law is not separable. Higher education sector, field of science 'Samfundsvidenskab' (social sciences) - law is not a separate field in Danmarks Statistik's classification - and all scientific staff (PERSONKAT=110), because no staff-category (professor) breakdown is tabulated. The ministry's datavarehus scientific-staff series is by hovedomraade only, without grade.

entity: EE: full professors of law (Statistics Estonia; HaridusSilm, Ministry of Education and Research)
notes: Statistics Estonia publishes no higher-education academic-staff table (only institution, enrolment, graduate and dropout tables); its R&D tables classify staff as researchers/technicians with no professor category. HaridusSilm, the ministry's official education-statistics portal, renders EHIS staff data only through an embedded Power BI report with no static table, download or API. No national figure for professors of law, or for professors or academic staff by field, is published.

entity: ES: professors of law (not separable in official statistics)
notes: Value left blank: the only published figure is 3,577 catedraticos de universidad in the whole Ciencias Sociales y Juridicas branch, which also covers economics, business, sociology and political science. EPU/SIIU table 'PDI en centros propios de universidades públicas por categoría, sexo y rama de enseñanza': 'Funcionario: Catedrático de Universidad', rama 'Ciencias Sociales y Jurídicas', ambos sexos, curso 2024-2025 = 3 577; law cannot be separated — the rama also covers economics, business, sociology, political science, etc. (EPU publishes law only as individual áreas de conocimiento, never as a 'Derecho' total); covers public universities' own centres only, private universities and attached centres excluded

entity: FI: professors of law (not separable in official statistics)

entity: FR: professeurs des universites, droit et science politique

entity: GR: professors of law (not separable in official statistics)

ELSTAT press release 'Tertiary Education (Universities and Technological Institutions) - End of Academic Year 2023/2024', 18 Dec 2025, Table 2 'Teaching staff by gender and educational institution', row Total: 19,372 (university education 18,841). entity: HR: full professors of law (Državni zavod za statistiku)
notes: DZS release OBR-2025-4-1 (academic year 2024/2025), tables 1-4: academic staff by university title, employment/contract basis, degree and sex. Full professors nationally = 3,471 (2,822 on employment contracts). No breakdown by znanstveno polje, so professors of law are not separately published.

entity: HU: full professors of law (Központi Statisztikai Hivatal)
notes: KSH Magyar statisztikai évkönyv 2024, table 3.6.16 Felsőoktatás: lecturers by post only; egyetemi és főiskolai tanár (professors) = 2,179 in 2024/2025, all disciplines. Tables 3.6.17-3.6.18 break students and graduates down by képzési terület but no table crosses academic post with field, so professors of law are not published.

entity: IE: academic staff in arts, humanities, social sciences, business and law (Higher Education Authority)
notes: HEA staff data classify academic staff only as AHSSBL / STEMM / OTHER and publish them per institution with no system-level total, so no single published figure exists and categories may not be summed here. entity: LT: professors of law (not separable in official statistics)
notes: Value left blank: the published 8,773 is university lecturers in all fields, all ranks, not professors of law. SDMX dataflow S3R527 'University lecturers' (M3110712), academic year 2025-2026, code 'destytojai' = lecturers in main and second job, persons, universities only (excludes colleges). Main job only: 5,270. The statistical database publishes no professorial-rank dimension and no field-of-science dimension, so no law-specific or professor-only count exists. entity: LU: professorial staff, Department of Law
notes: Professorial staff of the law department, ranks not disaggregated; not full professors only. Department of Law Activity Report 2023, p.2: 'At the end of 2023, the Department has 27 professors, as well as 3 invited and honorary professors'. Department of Law is the country's law faculty (University of Luxembourg is the only university). The report does not disaggregate the 27 by full/associate/assistant rank, so this is the professorial staff, not full professors alone. STATEC publishes no higher-education teaching-staff table.

entity: LV: professors of law (not separable in official statistics)
notes: Value left blank: the published 606 is professors in all fields, not law. CSB table IGP040 'Academic staff (in main job) in tertiary education institutions by sex and elected position', occupation 'Professor', total, 2025. Main job only. No field-of-science breakdown is published for academic staff, so this is the whole-country professorial count, not law. Same table: 629 (2024), 604 (2023), 645 (2022).

entity: MT: professors of law (not separable in official statistics)
notes: Value left blank: the published 2,826 is tertiary academic staff in all fields. NSO 'Personnel in Education: 2023-2024', NR 208/2025, Table 3, tertiary education ISCED 5-8, academic year 2023-2024: total 2,826 (1,723 male, 1,103 female). Academic staff = tertiary personnel whose primary assignment is instruction, any rank from professor to assistant lecturer (methodological note 12), pro-rated across levels. entity: NL: professors of law (Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek)

entity: PL: professors of law (Główny Urząd Statystyczny)
notes: GUS 'Szkolnictwo wyższe i jego finanse w 2024 r.' (published 30.10.2025) reports academic teachers only by position/title and by voivodeship: table 3(45) gives 10 045 academic teachers holding the title of professor nationally, with no field or discipline breakdown; no GUS table of academic teachers by dziedzina/dyscyplina found in the 2023 or 2024 editions; RAD-on (POL-on) field-level data require authenticated access (API returned HTTP 401)

entity: PT: professors of law (not separable in official statistics)
notes: Value left blank: the published figure is 4,704 teaching staff in ISCED-F 04 business/administration/law, all ranks, and is not a law-professor count. Published field is ISCED-F 2013 area 04 'Ciencias empresariais, administracao e direito' (business, administration and law) in which law is not separable; the figure counts all higher-education teaching staff, not professors only. DGEEC data as disseminated by Statistics Portugal, academic year 2023/24 (last updated 2024-10-18). Total teachers all fields 41,361.

entity: RO: full professors of law (Institutul Naţional de Statistică)
notes: INS Tempo-Online is a matrix-selection interface that returns no data without interactive dimension selection, and insse.ro PDF publications returned HTTP 503. INS higher-education staffing series aggregate by institution and teaching grade rather than by faculty, so a per-law-faculty professor table was not located in any reachable INS output.

entity: SE: professors of law (FTE)
notes: 106.93 FTE rounded to 107; the source publishes full-time equivalents, not headcount. Research subject group 'Juridik' (law, within Social Sciences), employment category 'Professorer'. Reported in heltidsekvivalenter (full-time equivalents), which is the only subject-group breakdown UKAE/SCB publish - individuals are not published by subject group; hence the decimal. All subjects: 5,490.13 professor FTE. Reference date 2025.

entity: SI: full professors of law (Statistični urad Republike Slovenije)
notes: SURS tertiary-education staff series are not crossed by discipline: 0383508S gives participants and teaching/academic staff by category and level (2018-2020), 0953704S gives teaching staff by post and education (2007-2015). No table combines the title redni profesor with field of education (KLASIUS-P-16/ISCED-F), so a national count of law professors is not published.

entity: SK: professors of law (public law faculties)
notes: Sum of 4 law faculties published in one table: CVTI SR, Štatistická ročenka – vysoké školy 2025, Tab16 (učitelia na ustanovený pracovný čas, verejné vysoké školy, state at 31.10.2025), rank category 'profesori': Právnická fakulta UK 38 + PF UPJŠ 9 + PF UMB 9 + PF TTU 9 = 65. Same rank category, same year, full-time. Excludes private and state HEIs, which are published in separate tables (Tab16s, Tab16š); excludes docenti and odborní asistenti.

entity: FR: avocats aux Conseils (Ordre des avocats au Conseil d'État et à la Cour de cassation)
notes: Ministère de la Justice, Références statistiques Justice 2024, ch.3 table 1 (officiers publics et ministériels au 1er janvier 2024): avocats aux conseils total 125, of whom 107 associés, individual and salaried not disclosed; monopoly of representation before the Conseil d'État and the Cour de cassation (loi of 31 Dec 1971); no vacancies

entity: BE: avocats à la Cour de cassation (Ordre des avocats à la Cour de cassation de Belgique)
notes: Art. 484 Code judiciaire; one Ordre for the whole country, separate from OBFG/OVB; sole representatives in civil, commercial, social and disciplinary cassation (criminal and fiscal: not compulsory); the Tableau de l'Ordre at 1 April 2026 numbers 17 members, with 8 honorary listed separately; the Ordre publishes the tableau but no aggregate total, so 17 is the last-numbered entry of that official list rather than a stated figure

entity: DE: Rechtsanwälte beim Bundesgerichtshof (Rechtsanwaltskammer beim Bundesgerichtshof)
notes: Chamber's own admission page: 'Derzeit sind 43 Anwälte bei dem Bundesgerichtshof zugelassen'; singular admission (Singularzulassung) requiring age 35, five years' practice and selection by the Wahlausschuss, appointment by the Federal Minister of Justice; mandatory for revision proceedings in civil and criminal matters; the BRAK member statistic at 1 Jan 2024 recorded 37 (sources/official/probes/senadv_DE_brak_mitglieder_2024.pdf)

entity: DK: advokater med møderet for Højesteret (Advokatsamfundet)
notes: retsplejeloven § 134(1): an advokat obtains møderet for Højesteret on application with an Advokatrådet certificate (five years' practice with landsret møderet) and a landsret 'øvethedserklæring'; a formal right of audience inside one unified profession, not a separate bar; Advokatsamfundet publishes flows only (88 new landsret møderet in 2023) and no stock count of Højesteret møderet was located

entity: EE: no separate senior-advocate grade (Eesti Advokatuur)

entity: GR: no separate senior-advocate grade (Δικηγορικός Σύλλογος)

entity: ES: no separate senior-advocate grade (Consejo General de la Abogacía Española)
notes: Unified abogacía; procuradores represent and abogados plead before the Tribunal Supremo, but there is no separate senior or cassation grade with its own roll; the Abogado del Estado is a state legal corps, not a private senior bar

entity: FI: no separate senior-advocate grade (Suomen Asianajajaliitto)
notes: Unified asianajaja profession; any member of the Bar may act before the korkein oikeus; no cassation roll or senior grade

entity: IE: senior counsel (The Bar of Ireland)
notes: Bar of Ireland Annual Report 2023/24, Law Library membership at June 2024: senior counsel 362 (17%) of 2,097 members, gender split 73 F + 289 M; a second panel on the same page headlines 364 senior counsel, so the two published figures differ by two; counts Law Library members holding patents of precedence, not every patent-holding senior counsel; the live site returns HTTP 403 to automated clients, so this copy came from the Internet Archive snapshot of the same URL

entity: IT: avvocati iscritti all'albo speciale dei cassazionisti (Consiglio Nazionale Forense)
notes: CNF statistics for 2013: 55,494 enrolled in the albo speciale at 31 Dec 2013 (3,520 enrolments and 965 deletions during 2013); enrolment is required to plead before the Corte di cassazione and the other giurisdizioni superiori (art. 22 l. 247/2012); this is the latest machine-readable national total located - the CNF 2017 sheet is a scanned image and no newer national figure was found, so the row is a stale count, not the current one

entity: NL: advocaten bij de Hoge Raad (Nederlandse orde van advocaten)
